U: › informal a covering of short thin soft hairs, or a mass of tightly curled and often untidy hair
› UK and US old-fashioned slang or Australian English informal the police

example: He's got that bit of adolescent fuzz on his upper lip.
他的上嘴唇上長著些青春期的短鬚。
I must buy a razor today and get rid of the fuzz on my legs!
我今天必須買個剃鬚刀刮掉我腿上的絨毛。

NONE: › (of an image) having shapes that do not have clear edges, or (of a sound, especially from a television, radio, etc.) not clear, usually because of other unwanted noises making it difficult to hear
（圖像）模糊不清的；（聲音）雜亂的，有干擾的
› (of hair) in an untidy mass of tight curls
（毛髮）零亂的；有緊致的小卷的
› A fuzzy surface feels like short fur.

example: Is the picture always fuzzy on your TV?
你的電視一直這麽不清楚嗎？
You can pick up a lot of stations on the car radio but the sound is usually sort of fuzzy.
汽車上的收音機可以收到一大堆電臺，但聲音通常都會有些干擾。
The basic facts of the story are starting to emerge though the details are still fuzzy.
雖然一些細節仍然並不清晰，但事情的基本事實已經浮出水面了。
My head's a little fuzzy (= I cannot think clearly) this morning after all that wine last night.
昨天晚上喝了那麽多酒，今天早晨我有些不清醒。
Oh no, it's raining - my hair will get all fuzzy.
噢，不會吧，下雨了——我的頭髮會變得亂蓬蓬的。
the fuzzy skin of a peach

NONE: › a system of theories used in mathematics, computing, and philosophy to deal with statements that are neither true nor false
